structure: US personal (individual or business) fundraisers pay one transaction fee per donation of 2.9% + $0.30, deducted automatically from each donation before transfer; the recipient receives the donation minus that fee and there is no fee to create or manage a fundraiser (0% platform fee). US certified-nonprofit fundraisers are charged 2.2% + $0.30 per donation. Donor tips to GoFundMe are optional, charged to the donor on top of the donation (never deducted from the fundraiser), adjustable to any amount including 0, and the organizer cannot see them. If a donor chooses a recurring (monthly) donation, the donor pays an additional 5% fee per recurring donation (not applicable to GoFundMe Pro). International transaction and currency-conversion fees may apply depending on the donor's payment method. Rounding is not stated; the platform's own example resolves to exact cents ($50 -> $48.25).

examples.quote: If a donor makes a $50 donation to a US fundraiser, the individual receiving funds will receive $48.25 once transaction fees (2.9% + $0.30) are deducted.

quotes: One transaction fee 2.9% + $0.30 Automatically deducted from each donation, so you never have to worry about paying a bill. International transaction and conversion fees may apply based on your payment method. (pricing page, United States, 'Individual or business' tab)

If donors choose recurring donations, they pay a fee of 5% per donation to help make this feature possible for our community.

Supporters who choose to make a recurring donation to an individual or charity on GoFundMe pay a 5% fee per donation to help support this feature. This fee does not apply to recurring donations made through GoFundMe Pro.

Leaving a tip is not mandatory, and it can be changed to any amount, including 0.
Your total due today will be the donation plus the amount you choose to tip.

Country mapping on the pricing page comes from its country selector as rendered: United States -> Individual or business 2.9% + $0.30; Certified nonprofit 2.2% + $0.30. Do not confuse with Australia, whose individual rate is also 2.2% + $0.30 (GST included).

Charity rate: the current US pricing page shows 'Certified nonprofit' at 2.2% + $0.30; nonprofit tooling is otherwise sold as GoFundMe Pro (custom pricing, 'typically 2.2%–2.5% + $0.30', +1% Amex). The legacy GoFundMe Charity help page (charitysupport.gofundme.com) failed to load on three fetchers (TLS handshake failure); the 'Free tier 0% platform + 1.9% + $0.30 / Flex tier 3% platform + 2.2% + $0.30' figures visible only in search-engine snippets are UNVERIFIED and likely obsolete.

Recurring-donation 5% fee is charged to the donor (it appears under 'Extra or larger than expected charge on statement'), so the fundraiser's net per recurring donation is still donation minus 2.9% + $0.30 unless GoFundMe states otherwise; a calculator author must decide whether to display it as a donor-side cost.

Payment methods covered by the single transaction fee per the help article: credit, debit, ACH, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay (for most fundraisers).

structure: US-based sellers selling in USD pay no Depop selling fee. When paid through Depop Payments (Stripe), a payment-processing fee of 3.3% + $0.45 is charged on the item sale price plus shipping costs plus any applicable taxes (i.e., the buyer's full payment), once per transaction (a bundle counts as one transaction), and is deducted before the proceeds reach the seller's bank account. If a listing (or the whole shop via Boost Shop) is boosted, a 12% boosting fee applies on the item sale price excluding taxes, plus the shipping cost if the seller arranged their own shipping rather than using a Depop Shipping label; it is charged only when a buyer interacted with the boosted listing and bought within 28 days, and it applies to new listings from 23 March 2026. All fees are reversed if the sale is refunded. Buyers separately pay a Marketplace fee (up to 5% of item price + up to $1, excluding taxes and shipping) that is not deducted from the seller.

structure: Listing is free. After a sale, Poshmark deducts its fee from the 'final order price' (the order/item price after seller discounts; buyer-paid shipping and sales tax are outside this base): a flat $2.95 when the sale is under $15, or 20% (seller keeps 80%) when the sale is $15 or above. The buyer pays a flat $6.49 shipping fee for a USPS Ground Advantage label covering the order (or a bundle from one closet) up to 5 lb; above 5 lb the seller pays, buying a heavier-weight label upgrade at $5.00 (5.1–10 lb) or $10.00 (10.1–15 lb), paying only the difference from the original label. Since October 1, 2025, sellers with a Texas return address also have a Texas Seller Fee Tax deducted: Texas state (6.25%) plus local sales tax applied to 80% of Poshmark's fee. Rounding rules are not published.

rates.selling_fee_base: item price + buyer-paid shipping (listings created or updated on/after 2025-01-06)

structure: For listings created or updated on or after January 6, 2025, the seller pays a flat 10% selling fee on the combined item price plus buyer-paid shipping; no separate payment-processing fee is charged to either side. The buyer pays a 3.6% Buyer Protection fee on the same base (item price + buyer-paid shipping), shown in the checkout total and not deducted from the seller. Legacy listings created before January 6, 2025 and never updated carry the old structure instead: no seller fee, but the buyer pays a 10% service fee and a payment-processing fee of $0.50 + 2.9% of the transaction price (item + shipping + service fee + sales tax). Payouts: ACH direct deposit is free (once per day; $2 for each failed request); Instant Pay costs a flat $3 per cash-out (once per day, up to $600/month). Rounding is not published.

notes: Timeline (official): March 2024 — seller fees removed and a buyer service fee introduced ('When we initially introduced our current fee structure in March ... sellers got to keep 100% of their sales proceeds'); January 6, 2025 — 10% selling fee reinstated, 3.6% Buyer Protection fee introduced, payment-processing fee dropped for new/updated listings, $2 ACH cash-out fee removed at 2:00 PM PT; January 6–12, 2025 — transition week with no 10% fee on old-structure listings; May 7, 2026 — prepaid USPS label rates changed for the fuel surcharge (fee page 'Updated 05/07/2026'). No 2026 change to the 10% / 3.6% structure appears on official pages.
Conflict: several third-party pages date the reinstated 10% fee to 'January 6, 2026' — UNVERIFIED and contradicted by Mercari's own pages, which say January 6, 2025.

Calculator ambiguity: the fee base is 'item price + buyer-paid shipping'. When the seller offers free shipping there is no buyer-paid shipping in the base, and the label cost comes out of the seller's proceeds (label prices from the rate table); when the buyer pays shipping via a Mercari label, the fee is 10% of item + shipping even though the shipping money passes through to the carrier.

Legacy structure applies only to listings created before Jan 6, 2025 that were never updated; Mercari said existing listings would be 'updated automatically within a week', so it should be rare in 2026.

Instant Pay details ($3 flat, $600/month, once per day, up to 30 minutes) come from the fee page; the dedicated Instant Pay how-to article (article 93) is JavaScript-rendered and returned an empty body to HTTP fetchers.

rates.sell_more_earn_more_us_test_tiers: US Fashion / Toys & Hobbies / Food & Drink only, by trailing 4-week total sales: $0 Standard 8.00%; $20,000 Tier 1 7.00%; $35,000 Tier 2 6.00%; $50,000 Tier 3 5.00%; $100,000 Tier 4 4.00%; $250,000 Tier 5 3.75%; $500,000 Tier 6 3.50%; $1,000,000 Tier 7 3.25%; $1,500,000 Tier 8 3.00%; Coins & Money 4% at all tiers; all other categories 8% at all tiers; runs through at least 2026-11-01

structure: Two fees are deducted per checkout transaction. Commission is a percentage of the item's final sale price (accepted offer/auction price after seller-generated coupons), excluding shipping and taxes: 8% in most US categories, 4% for Coins & Money (Coins & Bullion, Paper Money & Currency) and for the Pallets wholesale category (limited time). Payment processing is 2.9% of the total order value paid by the buyer at checkout (item + buyer-paid shipping + buyer-paid sales tax) plus a fixed $0.30 per transaction; it therefore varies with shipping and tax even for identical item prices. Since January 14, 2026, in select categories (Comics & Anime, Toys & Hobbies, Coins & Money, Trading Card Games, Entertainment Cards, Sports Singles subcategories, and from June 4, 2026 Bags & Accessories and Jewelry & Watches) the commission is 0% on the portion of an individual order's price above $1,500 while processing still applies to the full amount; sports breaks and surprise products are excluded. Net earnings = final sale price − commission − payment processing − any state tax on fees − any seller-covered shipping. Whatnot-issued coupons do not reduce the seller's price; giveaways carry no seller fees. The same schedule applies to live shows and marketplace (non-live) listings; for live sales the rate follows the show's category, for marketplace sales the product's category.

notes: Live vs marketplace: the fee schedule does not differentiate live-show sales from marketplace (Buy It Now/offer) sales; the only stated difference is which category sets the rate (show category for live, product category for marketplace).

Trading cards: Trading Card Games, Entertainment Cards and Sports Singles have the standard 8% commission but qualify for the 0%-above-$1,500 promotion; sports breaks and Surprise Products do not. Coins & Money is the only permanently reduced category (4%); Pallets (wholesale) is 4% 'limited time'.

Electronics: the 'Reduced Commission on Electronics' article now returns 404 and Electronics is not a reduced row in the fee table; search-engine snippets citing a 5% electronics commission are stale/unverified. The snippet 'Seller fees are ≤8% (varies by category/country)' also comes from an older revision of the fee page.

The high-value 0% promotion has no stated end date ('limited time'; Whatnot may end it at any time). Sell More, Earn More is a US-only test for a subset of sellers through at least November 1, 2026; a calculator should treat tiered rates as optional/conditional.

Payment processing uses the buyer's total including sales tax, so an exact fee needs shipping and buyer tax as inputs; in Whatnot's own example 2.9% × $58.70 + $0.30 = $2.0023 is shown as $2.00 (rounded to cents).

Taxes on fees: sellers in DC, HI, NM, WV pay state sales tax on the commission; sellers in CT (special 1% rate), HI, NM, OH, SD, TX (rate reduced by 20%), WV pay it on the payment-processing fee; these are deducted from earnings.

structure: Sellers pay nothing to list or sell: after an order completes, the full agreed item price is credited to the seller's Vinted Wallet, and withdrawals to a US bank account (USD only) are free, take up to 5 business days, and require a minimum of $0.10. The buyer pays, on top of the item price, shipping and any sales tax, a mandatory Buyer Protection fee of $0.70 plus 5% of the item price (for a bundle, 5% of the combined bundle price, with the fixed part once per order); the help center says the fee is 'usually 5% + $0.70' and can vary by item characteristics, order value and order type. Shipping costs are borne by the buyer; taxes on integrated labels are paid by the buyer, while for custom shipping the applicable taxes are borne by the seller. Optional seller-paid item bumps are priced at checkout (3 or 7 calendar days) and are not refundable. For US–UK cross-border orders the buyer pays the same Buyer Protection fee and a 1.2% currency conversion built into the checkout exchange rate; the seller is paid in USD.
quotes: There are no fees for uploading your items or selling them on Vinted. This means once your sale is successfully closed, you'll receive the full selling price straight to your Vinted Wallet.
The Buyer will be automatically charged a Buyer Protection Fee for these Buyer Protection Services, which will always be shown at checkout before completion of the order.

The Buyer Protection Fee is calculated as follows: A fixed amount of $0.70; plus 5% of the item price agreed to between the Buyer and the Seller, not including the shipping costs, any additional costs and applicable taxes.
This fee is mandatory for every order made through Vinted and is added automatically at checkout.
The Buyer Protection fee typically includes a percentage of the item's or bundle's price, as well as a fixed fee — usually 5% + $0.70.
The calculation of this fee varies based on several factors, such as: item characteristics, order value, order type (a single item versus a bundle)
These shipping costs are borne by the Buyer, and they are displayed when the Seller provides that option to Buyers.
Taxes on Integrated shipping labels are paid by the Buyer, and for custom shipping, the applicable taxes are borne by the Seller.
The Fee for Bumping Listed Items is displayed before completion of the Bump order. Any applicable sales tax may also be added at checkout.
They can take up to 5 business days to arrive in your bank account (Monday–Friday, not including weekends and holidays).
You can withdraw earnings in dollars (USD) to supported accounts in banks or other financial institutions using account and routing numbers.
The minimum amount you can withdraw is $0.10. Withdrawals below this amount will fail.
When making international purchases on Vinted, the same Buyer Protection fee applies as for domestic transactions.
Our payment provider applies a 1.2% currency conversion fee to USD↔GBP transactions, which is included in the conversion rate provided at the checkout.
Item Verification is currently available in France, Italy, Belgium, Germany, Spain, The Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Denmark, Sweden, Lithuania and Finland.
The service fee is paid for by buyers and is visible on the item page and the checkout.
